skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // PhysicalAddress — Specifications
5. //
6. // A `PhysicalAddress` abstracts to a single mathematical integer: the raw
7. // physical address (`PhysicalAddress@ : int`, defined by the `View` impl in
8. // `phys.rs`, delegating to the inner `VirtualAddress`). The only derived notion
9. // callers reason about is the *frame* the address lies in
10. // (`addr / FRAME_SIZE == addr >> FRAME_SHIFT`), used to index the frame
11. // allocator's bitmaps / refcount arrays.
12. //
13. // Trust-boundary helpers pin the not-yet-verified `arch` `FrameNumber` type and
14. // the `arch`/`sys` library-edge constants/methods this module calls. They mirror
15. // the existing `sys`/`arch` `assume_specification` boundaries the codebase
16. // already draws (`::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` in `frame.rs`, the `Address` trait
17. // methods in `page.spec.rs` / `kframe.spec.rs`). `spec_page_size()` is the
18. // canonical frame size, re-exported from `crate::hal::mem` (defined alongside
19. // `FrameAddress`); `FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE == spec_page_size()`.
20. 
21. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
22. verus! {
23. 
24. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
25. use vstd::arithmetic::power2::pow2;
26. use vstd::arithmetic::div_mod::{
27.     lemma_fundamental_div_mod,
28.     lemma_mod_division_less_than_divisor,
29.     lemma_div_by_multiple,
30.     lemma_mod_multiples_basic,
31. };
32. use vstd::bits::lemma_usize_shr_is_div;
33. 
34. // `FrameNumber` lives in the `arch` crate, which is not Verus-enabled and has no
35. // `View`/datatype registration reachable here. Declare it to Verus as an opaque
36. // external datatype so it may appear in spec-fn parameters and the
37. // `assume_specification`s below. Its internals are not modeled (`external_body`):
38. // its abstract index is projected by `spec_frame_raw_value`.
39. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
40. #[verifier::external_body]
41. pub struct ExFrameNumber(FrameNumber);
42. 
43. // ── Frame-number trust-boundary projections (arch `FrameNumber`) ──────────────
44. //
45. // `FrameNumber` lives in the `arch` crate, which is not Verus-enabled and has no
46. // `View` impl reachable here (orphan rule). Its abstract index is therefore
47. // projected by an uninterpreted ghost function, exactly as `view_design.md`
48. // prescribes. `spec_max_frame_number()` denotes `FrameNumber::MAX`.
49. 
50. // The integer index of a frame number (`0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()`).
51. pub uninterp spec fn spec_frame_raw_value(frame: FrameNumber) -> int;
52. 
53. // The largest representable frame number. Mirrors `arch FrameNumber::MAX ==
54. // MAX_ADDRESS / FRAME_SIZE - 1 == usize::MAX / FRAME_SIZE - 1`. Interpreting it
55. // against `usize::MAX` and `spec_page_size()` is what lets verified constructors
56. // discharge their `usize` multiply (no-overflow) obligation: a frame index in
57. // `0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()` scaled by `spec_page_size()` stays `<= usize::MAX`.
58. pub open spec fn spec_max_frame_number() -> int {
59.     usize::MAX as int / spec_page_size() - 1
60. }
61. 
62. // ── Derived spec helpers over the View domain (`int`) ─────────────────────────
63. 
64. // The frame an address lies in: exact integer division, independent of whether
65. // the implementation shifts (`>> FRAME_SHIFT`) or divides (`/ FRAME_SIZE`).
66. pub open spec fn spec_frame_number(addr_view: int) -> int {
67.     addr_view / spec_page_size()
68. }
69. 
70. // The base (frame-aligned) address of a frame index: `frame * FRAME_SIZE`.
71. pub open spec fn spec_from_number(frame_view: int) -> int {
72.     frame_view * spec_page_size()
73. }
74. 
75. // ── `arch`/`sys` library-edge `assume_specification`s ─────────────────────────
76. 
77. // `::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE` is the frame size (alias of `PAGE_SIZE`), tied to the
78. // canonical `spec_page_size()`. It is strictly positive (`== 4096`); positivity is
79. // the load-bearing fact for the division/modulo reasoning in the constructors.
80. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE ] -> (result: usize)
81.     ensures
82.         result == spec_page_size(),
83.         spec_page_size() > 0,
84. ;
85. 
86. // `::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT == log2(FRAME_SIZE)`. Bounded below the pointer width
87. // so `raw_addr >> FRAME_SHIFT` is well-defined, and `2^FRAME_SHIFT == FRAME_SIZE`
88. // so the shift coincides with division by `spec_page_size()`.
89. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT ] -> (result: usize)
90.     ensures
91.         result < usize::BITS,
92.         pow2(result as nat) == spec_page_size(),
93. ;
94. 
95. // `VirtualAddress::new` is a pure newtype constructor: the wrapped value is the
96. // abstract address. (`sys` library edge; the inner module is not yet verified.)
97. pub assume_specification[ VirtualAddress::new ](value: usize) -> (result: VirtualAddress)
98.     ensures
99.         result@ == value as int,
100. ;
101. 
102. // `<VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value` is pure newtype identity: the
103. // returned raw `usize` equals the abstract address.
104. pub assume_specification[ <VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value ](
105.     addr: VirtualAddress,
106. ) -> (result: usize)
107.     ensures
108.         result as int == addr@,
109. ;
110. 
111. // `FrameNumber::into_raw_value` projects a frame number to its index; every
112. // `FrameNumber` value is in range (`0 ..= MAX`) by construction.
113. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::into_raw_value ](frame: FrameNumber) -> (result: usize)
114.     ensures
115.         result as int == spec_frame_raw_value(frame),
116.         0 <= spec_frame_raw_value(frame) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
117. ;
118. 
119. // `FrameNumber::from_raw_value` succeeds iff `value <= MAX`, preserving the index.
120. pub assume_specification[ FrameNumber::from_raw_value ](value: usize) -> (result: Option<FrameNumber>)
121.     ensures
122.         match result {
123.             Some(f) => value as int <= spec_max_frame_number()
124.                 && spec_frame_raw_value(f) == value as int,
125.             None => value as int > spec_max_frame_number(),
126.         },
127. ;
128. 
129. // ── Type invariant ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130. //
131. // Every `PhysicalAddress` a verified constructor produces has a *representable
132. // frame number*: `self@ / FRAME_SIZE <= FrameNumber::MAX`. This is the load-
133. // bearing fact that makes `into_frame_number` total (its internal
134. // `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` never panics), which the frame
135. // allocator relies on when using the result directly as a bitmap / refcount
136. // index. It is *not* alignment (MMIO addresses may be unaligned) and *not*
137. // RAM-validity (`from_mmio_address` deliberately bypasses that check).
138. impl PhysicalAddress {
139.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
140.         spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()
141.     }
142. }
143. 
144. } // verus!
145.

5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================

9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]

12. include!("phys.proof.rs");

15.     Address,
16.     FrameAddress,
17.     VirtualAddress,
18. };

21.     paging::FrameNumber,
22. };

37. ///
38. /// # Description
39. ///
40. /// A type that represents a physical address.
41. ///
42. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
43. #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
44. pub struct PhysicalAddress(VirtualAddress);
45. 
46. //==================================================================================================
47. // Implementations
48. //==================================================================================================
49. 
50. impl PhysicalAddress {
51.     pub fn from_virtual_address(addr: VirtualAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
52.         // Delegate to the per-platform validator to support sparse physical memory layouts.
53.         if !crate::hal::platform::is_valid_physical_address(addr) {
54.             return Err(Error::new(
55.                 ErrorCode::BadAddress,
56.                 "address out of bounds of physical memory",
57.             ));
58.         }
59. 
60.         Ok(Self(addr))
61.     }
62. 
63.     pub fn into_virtual_address(self) -> VirtualAddress {
64.         self.0
65.     }
66. 
67.     ///
68.     /// # Description
69.     ///
70.     /// Constructs a [`PhysicalAddress`] from a [`FrameAddress`].
71.     ///
72.     /// # Parameters
73.     ///
74.     /// - `frame_addr`: The frame address.
75.     ///
76.     /// # Returns
77.     ///
78.     /// A [`PhysicalAddress`] associated with the given `frame_addr`.
79.     ///
80.     pub fn from_frame_address(frame_addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
81.         let raw_addr: usize = frame_addr.into_raw_value() << mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
82.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(raw_addr))
83.     }
84. 
85.     pub fn from_into_frame_address(frame_addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
86.         let raw_addr: usize = frame_addr.into_raw_value() << mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
87.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(raw_addr))
88.     }
89. }
90. 
91. // Verification-target methods. They live in a dedicated `#[verus_verify]` impl
92. // block so that only the in-scope functions are checked (the self-less
93. // associated functions `from_mmio_address` / `from_number` require an enclosing
94. // `#[verus_verify]` impl to resolve), while the untouched constructors above are
95. // left out of verification scope.
96. #[verus_verify]
97. impl PhysicalAddress {
98.     ///
99.     /// # Description
100.     ///
101.     /// Constructs a physical address from a memory-mapped I/O address.
102.     ///
103.     /// # Parameters
104.     ///
105.     /// - `addr`: The memory-mapped I/O address.
106.     ///
107.     /// # Return Values
108.     ///
109.     /// Upon success, a physical address associated with the given memory-mapped I/O address is
110.     /// returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
111.     ///
112.     /// # Safety
113.     ///
114.     /// Behavior is undefined if the provided memory-mapped I/O address is invalid.
115.     ///
116.     // Deliberately bypasses the RAM-range validity check (MMIO GPAs may lie
117.     // outside tracked RAM). On success it is pure identity wrapping
118.     // (`r@ == addr@`); the `unsafe` contract — that `addr` denotes a valid MMIO
119.     // frame — is encoded as `requires` (frame-representability) so the result
120.     // satisfies the type invariant and may later flow into `into_frame_number`.
121.     #[verus_spec(result =>
122.         requires
123.             spec_frame_number(addr@) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
124.         ensures
125.             result is Ok,
126.             result matches Ok(r) ==> r@ == addr@ && r.inv(),
127.     )]
128.     pub unsafe fn from_mmio_address(addr: VirtualAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
129.         Ok(Self(addr))
130.     }
131. 
132.     ///
133.     /// # Description
134.     ///
135.     /// Constructs a [`PhysicalAddress`] from a [`FrameNumber`].
136.     ///
137.     /// # Parameters
138.     ///
139.     /// - `frame`: The frame number.
140.     ///
141.     /// # Returns
142.     ///
143.     /// A [`PhysicalAddress`] associated with the given `frame_number`.
144.     ///
145.     // The produced address is the frame's base address (`frame * FRAME_SIZE`).
146.     // The result is page-aligned (`result@ % FRAME_SIZE == 0`) and carries the
147.     // type invariant (`result.inv()`), so its sole caller can build a `FrameAddress`
148.     // (alignment) and later project it back with `into_frame_number` (`inv()`).
149.     #[verus_spec(result =>
150.         ensures
151.             result@ == spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(frame)),
152.             result@ % spec_page_size() == 0,
153.             result.inv(),
154.     )]
155.     pub fn from_number(frame: FrameNumber) -> Self {
156.         let frame_raw: usize = frame.into_raw_value();
157.         let page_size: usize = mem::FRAME_SIZE;
158.         proof! {
159.             // No-overflow: `frame_raw * page_size <= usize::MAX`. With
160.             // `frame_raw <= usize::MAX / page_size - 1` and `page_size > 0`, the
161.             // product stays within `usize`.
162.             let p: int = spec_page_size();
163.             let fr: int = spec_frame_raw_value(frame);
164.             let m: int = usize::MAX as int;
165.             lemma_fundamental_div_mod(m, p);
166.             lemma_mod_division_less_than_divisor(m, p);
167.             assert(p * (m / p) <= m);
168.             assert(fr * p <= m) by (nonlinear_arith)
169.                 requires
170.                     p > 0,
171.                     fr >= 0,
172.                     fr <= m / p - 1,
173.                     p * (m / p) <= m,
174.             ;
175.         }
176.         let addr: usize = frame_raw * page_size;
177.         proof! {
178.             // Alignment and invariant follow from `(fr * p) / p == fr <= MAX`.
179.             lemma_mod_multiples_basic(spec_frame_raw_value(frame), spec_page_size());
180.             lemma_div_by_multiple(spec_frame_raw_value(frame), spec_page_size());
181.         }
182.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(addr))
183.     }
184. 
185.     // Total projection: yields the containing frame (`self@ / FRAME_SIZE`). The
186.     // receiver's invariant guarantees the computed index fits a `FrameNumber`,
187.     // so the internal `unwrap()` never panics.
188.     #[verus_spec(result =>
189.         requires
190.             self.inv(),
191.         ensures
192.             spec_frame_raw_value(result) == spec_frame_number(self@),
193.     )]
194.     pub fn into_frame_number(self) -> FrameNumber {
195.         let raw_addr: usize = self.0.into_raw_value();
196.         let shift: usize = mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
197.         proof! {
198.             // `raw_addr >> shift == raw_addr / 2^shift == self@ / spec_page_size()`,
199.             // which `self.inv()` bounds by `spec_max_frame_number()`, so the index
200.             // is representable and `from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` is total.
201.             lemma_usize_shr_is_div(raw_addr, shift);
202.         }
203.         let frame_number: usize = raw_addr >> shift;
204.         // Safety: the following unwrap is safe because a physical address has a valid frame number.
205.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(frame_number).unwrap()
206.     }
